interest: This file provides valuable archival insight into the administrative mechanisms and financial controls governing foreign nationals and diplomatic/commercial agents on the eve of the Pacific War. It documents how taxation was leveraged as an instrument of exit control and border regulation, showing that foreigners departing Japan were required to settle premature income tax assessments, rent, and severance gratuities before obtaining exit permits, while the United States enforced reciprocal income tax clearance certificates for departing Japanese agents. Additionally, it illustrates the U.S. government's monitoring of Japanese wartime domestic fiscal legislation and its reliance on commercial translation organizations like The Okuyama Service in Tokyo to analyze major statutory revisions.
keywords: Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce
overview: This file comprises Department of State 'List of Papers' index and docket sheets for decimal file 894.5123, relating to income tax and taxation conditions in Japan during 1940 and 1941. The sheets record and summarize three individual sub-files (sub-numbers 54, 55, and 56). Sub-number 54 records a despatch from George A. Makinson in Tokyo transmitting an English translation from The Okuyama Service of Japan's revised Income Tax Law (Law No. 24, published in the Official Gazette on March 29, 1940) for transmission to the Finance Division of the Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce. Sub-numbers 55 and 56 are cross-reference notes (referencing file 894.56/82): sub-number 55 details Japanese regulations requiring foreign nationals departing Japan to produce tax receipts (including advance assessments for the current financial year), rent receipts, staff gratuities, and retirement allowances to obtain departure permits; sub-number 56 records a note by Frank A. Schuler, Jr. of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs concerning certificates of income tax compliance required of Japanese agents departing the United States.

subfiles.summary: This List of Papers docket sheet (Form DS-55) indexes sub-numbers 54 and 55 under decimal file 894.5123 concerning Japanese income taxation. Sub-number 54, dated October 14, 1940, from George A. Makinson in Tokyo, transmits a translation of Law No. 24 (the revised Income Tax Law of Japan, originally published in the Official Gazette on March 29, 1940) published by The Okuyama Service for transmission to the Finance Division of the Bureau of Foreign and Domestic Commerce. Sub-number 55 records a British Embassy despatch of September 8 (cross-referenced to 894.56/82) reporting that foreigners leaving Japan must obtain tax receipts, including prepayments for the current financial year's income tax, rent, and staff retiring allowances at Japanese rates, before receiving exit permits.

subfiles.about: Department of State List of Papers sheet recording an entry regarding tax compliance certificates required of Japanese agents leaving the United States.
subfiles.summary: This List of Papers sheet (page 48) records sub-number 56 under decimal file 894.5123. Dated September 16, 1941, the entry refers to a communication from Frank A. Schuler, Jr. of the State Department's Division of Far Eastern Affairs and cross-references file 894.56/82. It notes that Japanese agents departing the United States are required to obtain a certificate of compliance certifying payment of U.S. income tax prior to departure, though compliance certificates are not required for other taxes.
